reverification_cadence: quarterly, and on any provision-change event from the daily reg-watch detector
publisher: Council of AI (CSOAI Ltd, UK Companies House 16939677)
corrections_policy: appended, never edited — a wrong date here is a published correction, not a silent fix
scope_note: A cited deadline is regulatory context, not a determination that a person, model, or organisation is compliant.
headline_correction: The EU AI Act's high-risk obligations did NOT take effect 2 August 2026: the Digital Omnibus (Reg (EU) 2026/1744, in force 27 July 2026) deferred stand-alone Annex III high-risk to 2 December 2027 and product-embedded Annex I high-risk to 2 August 2028.
mirror_note: Client-side mirror of functions/api/regulation.ts REGULATION_FEED — same schema, same dates, byte-identical entries where the two overlap; the signed server feed at GET /api/regulation is the authority. One entry is carried client-side pending inclusion in the server register and is marked client_addition: the 2027-02-02 Code-of-Practice interoperability target for machine-readable marking (cross-referenced by the detector-interop axis note, 'Code-of-Practice target 2 Feb 2027').

deadlines.what: Article 5 prohibited practices + Article 4 AI literacy duties in force
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to €35,000,000 or 7% of worldwide annual turnover (EU AI Act Art 99(3))

deadlines.what: GPAI model provider obligations (Arts 53–55) + governance rules in force
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to €15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (EU AI Act Art 99(4))

deadlines.what: Mandatory AI-generated content labelling (visible + implicit metadata/watermark)
deadlines.penalty_exposure: CAC enforcement under the labelling measures; no fixed statutory maximum published

deadlines.what: Intent-based prohibitions, AG-exclusive enforcement, 60-day cure
deadlines.penalty_exposure: $10,000–$200,000 per violation plus up to $40,000/day continuing (HB 149)

deadlines.what: Transparency in Frontier AI Act — large frontier developers (> $500M revenue)
deadlines.penalty_exposure: AG-enforced civil penalties up to $1,000,000 per violation (Ch. 138, Statutes of 2025)

deadlines.what: High-impact + generative AI obligations; extraterritorial representative duty; one-year fine grace
deadlines.penalty_exposure: administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000 (~US$20,700) per Art 43; MSIT one-year fine grace in 2026

deadlines.what: Article 50 transparency + full penalty/market-surveillance regime + AI Office GPAI enforcement in force (NOT high-risk — see deferral)
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to €15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (EU AI Act Art 99(4))

deadlines.what: Large GenAI providers: public AI-detection tool plus manifest and latent disclosure for AI-generated media
deadlines.penalty_exposure: civil penalties enforceable by state authorities; no private right of action (SB 942/AB 853)

deadlines.what: Article 14 vulnerability/incident reporting live (24h early warning / 72h notification via ENISA Single Reporting Platform; covers legacy products)
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to €15,000,000 or 2.5% of worldwide annual turnover (CRA)

deadlines.what: Marking grace ends for generative systems placed on market before 2 Aug 2026
deadlines.basis: Art 111(4), inserted by Digital Omnibus Reg (EU) 2026/1744 Art 1(39)(b)
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to €15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (EU AI Act Art 99(4)(g))

deadlines.what: Prohibitions on AI generating non-consensual intimate imagery and CSAM take effect
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to €35,000,000 or 7% of worldwide annual turnover (EU AI Act Art 99(3), prohibited-practice tier)

deadlines.what: Member-state transposition deadline — software and AI enter strict no-fault liability
deadlines.penalty_exposure: no statutory cap — exposure is claimant-proven damage

deadlines.what: Automated-decision transparency obligation takes effect
deadlines.penalty_exposure: OAIC enforcement under the Privacy Act civil-penalty regime

deadlines.what: Frontier-developer disclosure statements begin (audit mandate follows 2028-01-01)
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to $1,000,000 first violation / $3,000,000 subsequent, plus $1,000/day for unfiled disclosures

deadlines.what: Frontier transparency + 72-hour incident reporting to NYDFS oversight office
deadlines.penalty_exposure: NYAG civil penalties up to $1,000,000 first / $3,000,000 subsequent

deadlines.what: ADMT disclosure/transparency framework (replaces repealed SB 24-205)
deadlines.penalty_exposure: Colorado AG enforcement; no fixed statutory maximum published

deadlines.instrument: EU AI Act Art 50(2) — Code of Practice
deadlines.what: Code-of-Practice target for interoperable machine-readable marking (watermark interop) of AI-generated content — detectors from different providers are expected to read each other's marks
deadlines.basis: Reg (EU) 2024/1689 Art 50(2) + Art 56 Code of Practice — https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to €15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (EU AI Act Art 99(4)(g))

deadlines.what: Pre-Aug-2025 GPAI models must reach compliance; national regulatory-sandbox obligation
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to €15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (EU AI Act Art 99(4))

deadlines.what: Stand-alone Annex III high-risk obligations apply (deferred from 2 Aug 2026)
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to €15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (EU AI Act Art 99(4))

deadlines.what: Mandatory annual independent third-party audits of frontier developers
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to $1,000,000 first violation / $3,000,000 subsequent, plus $1,000/day for unfiled disclosures

deadlines.what: Product-embedded Annex I high-risk obligations apply
deadlines.penalty_exposure: up to €15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (EU AI Act Art 99(4))

disputed.item: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (CETS 225) entry-into-force status
disputed.note: sources disagree as of the verification date; stated honestly rather than guessed

underwriting_note: Deadlines and cited penalty exposure can inform an underwriter; CSOAI does not underwrite, price risk, or determine legal compliance.
